subject: LLM origin decommission & serving priorities survey
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Priya Bhatia <priya.b@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-09-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Recap: today’s discovery — origin exit + serving needs (quick survey)

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great context on the timeline and the origin-exit pressure you’re dealing with. I promised a short written recap and two asks so we can land the right recommendation for you: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) plus migration constraints.

Recap (short):
- Current production: in-house GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100, mixed orchestration).
- Traffic: ~1.2M tokens/day, peak 240 concurrent requests; response SLA target ~300–500ms p50 for short chat.
- Data: some PII in prompts; legal requires data residency + strict audit logs for a subset of endpoints.
- Timeline: aim to decommission original cluster by end of Q1 2027.

Two quick asks (can reply inline):
1) Deployment preference today (select one or rank): Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private VPC/on-prem. If you pick Hosted, tell us which endpoints you’d want private routing/audit exceptions for.
2) Migration sources: are you moving from your legacy self-hosted model only, or also migrating traffic from a third-party LLM API (please name)? Any redlines re: code/weights transfer?

I attached the short inventory template — filling rows for each model variant will help us size Dedicated pools and estimate incremental latency for KV cache warmup.

Next steps I’ll take once I have your answers: map to a recommended serving lane, provide a rough cost delta (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and draft a mutual action plan with milestones for cutover.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0184
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme-llm-inventory.csv (CSV stub: model_name,weights_location,avg_seq_len,tokens/day)
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Bhatia <priya.b@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-09-11T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: today’s discovery — origin exit + serving needs (quick survey)

Thanks, Soojin — quick answers below. Filling the inventory now and will attach in a follow-up (should be by EOD tomorrow).

1) Deployment preference (ranked):
- #1 Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable latency + data isolation)
- #2 Private VPC (for sensitive endpoints only)
- #3 Hosted API (for low-sensitivity / exploratory endpoints)

Notes: we prefer Dedicated for the majority of production traffic because current SLA sensitivity and predictable cost are top priorities. For a handful (~10%) of endpoints handling higher-sensitivity PII we want Private VPC with KMS integration. Hosted is fine for non-PII dev/test traffic to speed up ramp.

2) Migration sources:
- Primary: legacy self-hosted cluster (weights are our IP; we will not hand over raw checkpoints).
- Secondary: some low-volume flows routed through third-party API (Open-API Inc) — we need a fallthrough strategy while we re-route calls.

Constraints / redlines: cannot export HSM-protected keys or share raw customer prompts with third parties. Audit logs are required for all Private and Dedicated hosts (retention 1 year).

Priya — adding you for any compliance clarifications.

Appreciate the quick turn here.

Samir
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Priya Bhatia <priya.b@acme.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T17:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: today’s discovery — origin exit + serving needs (quick survey)

Samir — perfect, thanks for the clear ranking. Looping in Ben (sales lead) and Marissa (solutions lead) so we can:
- Put together pricing for both Dedicated and a Private VPC bolt-on for the ~10% sensitive endpoints.
- Draft a migration playbook that leaves a short-lived API gateway to Open-API Inc traffic for fallthrough during cutover.

Ben / Marissa — quick asks:
- Ben: can you provide a range for a 12-month committed Dedicated pool sized for ~1.2M tokens/day with 240 peak concurrent requests (approx spec: 8x A100-equivalent)? Include options with 20% burst capacity + SLA.
- Marissa: can you confirm scope for Private VPC (KMS, audit logs retention 1 year, peered VPC) and an estimated 4-week integration timeline for our standard onboarding?

Samir — once I have those two inputs I’ll draft a mutual action plan with milestone dates for your Q1 2027 decommission. Proposed near-term milestone: inventory CSV + basic network allowlist by 2026-09-20.

Thanks — Soojin
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: today’s discovery — origin exit + serving needs (quick survey)

Samir — thanks for the context. At a high level:
- Ballpark monthly cost for a 12-month commit Dedicated pool (8x A100-equivalent, 20% burst): $47k–$62k / month depending on quantization profile and sustained concurrency.
- Hosted variant (for non-PII dev/test traffic): ~30–40% higher per-token on pay-as-you-go but no commit required.
- Private VPC add-on (KMS + 1yr audit retention + VPC peering): one-time onboarding fee $12k + $8k/month operational overlay.

I’ll attach a short pricing snapshot and a proposed mutual action plan template in a separate email (cc Marissa). For timing: we can produce a more detailed Dedicated sizing estimate once we get the completed inventory CSV and a sample traffic trace (a 48-hour window is ideal).

Action items (agreed):
- Acme: inventory CSV + allowlist — target 2026-09-20.
- Redwood: detailed Dedicated quote + Private VPC scoping doc — target 2026-09-22.
- All: follow-up call week of 2026-09-27 to review quote + M.A.P.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
